name: register_device_token

body.message: The device id field is required. (and 2 more errors)

device_id: The device id field is required.
device_token: The device token field is required.

body.message: Something went wrong. Please try again later.

side_effects: request OS notification permission only after the user accepts the dialog

open_questions.question: Should the app send device_id?
open_questions.answer: No. Removed for now (owner decision). Send only device_token (+ platform, token_type).

open_questions.question: When is the prompt shown, and what if the user declines?
open_questions.answer: After a successful login, once per install: show the dialog on the first dashboard visit after login. If declined, do not ask again and send nothing. (Default; confirm.)

open_questions.question: PushNotificationService.init() already calls requestPermission() at app start. Keep that?
open_questions.answer: No. Move the OS permission request into the accepted dialog so the user is not prompted twice. (Default; confirm.)

task_after_success: After login, show a dialog 'Turn on push notifications?'. Accept: request OS permission, read the FCM token from FirebaseMessaging (only when FirebaseBootstrap.isAvailable), then POST this endpoint with device_token (+ platform, token_type 'fcm' on Android, 'apns' on iOS) and NO device_id. Decline: do nothing. On failure (including the expected 422 on device_id) show nothing to the user and never block them; log it.
out_of_scope: No token refresh listener (onTokenRefresh) in this spec. Not part of login: login sends no device fields. Logout device removal is a separate spec. Do not generate or store a device_id.
known_issue: The backend reference lists device_id as REQUIRED (422 validation_failed on device_id when missing). Without it this call is expected to fail until the backend makes it optional or the app sends one. Treat a 422 here as non-fatal.
